4.why: Source P4: finish at the original belay where the Thin Red Line pendulum is; older SMC bolt left backed up by better anchor right; small ledge.
4.text: On a small ledge at the old belay where the Thin Red Line pendulum begins; clip the older bolt to the left and back it up to the better anchor on the right.

6.why: Source P6: ends on a ledge, anchor about 25 ft right at the height of Thin Red Line P7.
6.text: On a good ledge, with the anchor about 25 ft to the right, level with the seventh pitch of the neighbouring Thin Red Line.

11.why: Source P11: fixed three-nut anchor just above the trees; 'top of the corner' was not stated (route wanders to lower-angle ground first), so corrected.
11.text: At a fixed three-nut anchor just above the trees, reached by wandering onto lower-angle ground after the finger-crack corner.

P8.why: alpinedave P8 (blocky ramp): belay a full rope length up from the base of the wall; 'top of the ramp' was inference, corrected.
P8.text: A full rope length up from the base of the steep wall that the blocky ramp cuts through.

P9.why: alpinedave P9, the first 5.9 pitch, ends at a large ledge; numbering and content match stored.
P9.text: On the large ledge that tops the first 5.9 pitch.

P13-18.why: Combined label, source pitches 15-17 unnumbered (inferred); sentence mixes the trees/heather belay with the 'wall kicks back' belay and misstates the bush/heather positions.

1.why: MP P1: hand crack to a belay on a ledge atop the lowest pillar.
1.text: On a comfortable ledge on top of the lowest pillar, at the end of the hand crack.

2.why: MP P2: traverse face to a belay in the wide crack splitting the lower buttress.
2.text: Inside the wide crack that splits the lower buttress, after traversing the face leftward.

3.why: MP P3: pedestal at top of pillar beneath large diving-board block, medium nuts; 'beside' corrected.
3.text: On a pedestal at the top of the pillar, under a large diving-board block, with medium nuts for protection.

4.why: MP P4: belay in blocks in the middle of the buttress after the crack ends.
4.text: Among blocks near the middle of the buttress, once the crack ends and the ground turns blocky.

5.why: MP P5: belay under the block that forms a keyhole over the corner crack.
5.text: Directly under the block that caps the corner crack and forms a keyhole.

6.why: MP P6: chimney system exits onto the first-ascent bivy ledge, belay there.
6.text: Out on the bivy ledge used by the first ascent party, above the chimney system.

7.why: MP P7: belay at base of upper headwall; 60 m rope belay short and scramble ~10 m third class.
7.text: At the base of the upper headwall; on a 60 m rope stop short and scramble about 10 m of easy third class to reach it.

8.why: MP P8: ledge with old angle piton of doubtful quality, #6 cam belay; reworded to avoid close copying.
8.text: On a ledge with an old, doubtful angle piton; a #6 cam is convenient, otherwise use small gear and chockstones.

9.why: MP P9: belay in a corner at large blocks after the vertical hand crack.
9.text: In a corner among large blocks, above the vertical hand crack.
